claims.text: THE PROVENANCE SPLIT, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL FACT THE 19 SEPTEMBER 2026 PASS FOUND. Of 47 named nuclear-facility witnesses assembled in that pass, 26 reached the record through CONTEMPORANEOUS OFFICIAL PAPER: message traffic, memoranda for the record, NORAD and base operations duty logs, AF Form 117 questionnaires, a Project Blue Book telephone log and a wing historian's file. 13 reached it through A RESEARCHER'S INTERVIEW PROGRAMME. Of those 13, at least four reached it through ONE MAN'S interviews: Walter Figel, Frederick Meiwald, Robert Jamison and Robert J. Kaminski, all via Robert Hastings or Robert Salas. The remaining handful published under their own names before anyone sought them out. Only four of the 47 were on this board before the pass.

claims.text: WHY THAT SPLIT IS THE QUERY THE BOARD SHOULD BE ABLE TO RUN. The triage rule of 19 September 2026 asks for two questions to be askable: show convergences where at least one leg is documented, and separately show clusters where every leg is Tier 2 and trace whether they share a source. The 26-versus-13 split is the index that makes the second one answerable in this domain. The 26 are a control group. The four who share one interviewer are the cluster the second query is designed to catch, and CLAUDE.md section 2 governs them: four witnesses sharing a single interviewer are one method applied four times, not four independent confirmations.

The contemporaneous-paper half of that split is real and checkable. It includes the National Military Command Center's Memorandum for Record of 29 October 1975 on the Loring penetration; the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 7 to 19 November 1975; the Project Blue Book Minot file of October and November 1968 with seven AF Form 117 witness questionnaires; the Project Blue Book telephone log of 1 August 1965 for F. E. Warren; and the 379th Bombardment Wing historian's file of January 1979. All were opened by this board on 19 September 2026.

desc: The Atomic Energy Act creates the only category of information in American law that is classified from the instant it comes into existence, without any official act: Restricted Data, covering the design, manufacture and use of nuclear weapons and the production of special nuclear material. That regime is administered by the Department of Energy and the National Nuclear Security Administration rather than by the Department of Defense, runs on its own clearance system - Q and L access authorisations - and reports to different congressional committees. For a concealment architecture this is an alternative channel of considerable value: material characterised at a national laboratory under Restricted Data controls is protected by a statute rather than an executive order, is outside the SAP notification framework of 10 U.S.C. 119, and is audited by a different set of overseers. The documented convergence is that the laboratories that would perform the analysis - Los Alamos, Sandia, Oak Ridge, Livermore - are precisely the DOE complex, and AARO's own January 2026 materials analysis was in fact performed by Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Scoring high on this domain means an entity held Q clearance, worked the DOE complex, or exercised Restricted Data authority.
